Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Sudden-onset, persistent, severe unilateral/right-predominant headache for 3 days; photophobia; transient visual “shooting lights”; mild nausea; no focal neurologic deficits; on combined OCP; family history of migraine.  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura (status migrainosus) — supported by photophobia, visual aura, unilateral severe pain, partial response to NSAID, and positive family history.  
- Differential considerations (consistent with DDx):  
  • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) – medium likelihood given estrogen OCP use and persistent headache; needs exclusion if examination abnormal or headache worsens.  
  • Idiopathic intracranial hypertension – medium likelihood; consider if papilledema or raised ICP signs on exam.  
- Management:  
  • Prescribed stronger NSAID (exact drug/dose not documented) plus concurrent paracetamol; advise with food.  
  • Book in-person appointment for full neurological exam, BP measurement, and fundoscopy.  
  • Discussed potential need to change OCP if migraine with aura confirmed.  
  • Safety-net: attend ED if headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes in character.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine with visual aura – High likelihood: classic features (photophobia, visual aura, unilateral severe pain) and family history.  
2. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Medium likelihood: estrogen OCP use, new persistent severe headache, positional component.  
3. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension – Medium likelihood: female of child-bearing age on OCP with visual symptoms; needs optic-disc assessment.
